cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description: Hm. This will only match if the very last line has a line number but that's not always true since we sometimes bail out and just print the component name for that line. It's also possible that the root is a built-in component. E.g. `<Suspense>`. Those won't have a line number. It's probably likely that at least one of the frames has one but not guaranteed.

evidence.thread_resolution:
bvaughn: Right, this is not a perfect check but it's a fallback check. Do you have a better suggestion?
bvaughn: > It's also possible that the root is a built-in component. E.g. <Suspense>. Those won't have a line number. It's probably likely that at least one of the frames has one but not guaranteed.

Since the component stack is reverse, the "first" item would be a user component anyway- but this should match an entry on a line other than the first regardless.

I'm banking on there being at least one line with source info, or we won't have a way to differentiate between a stack and an arbitrary string.
sebmarkbage: `/:\d+:\d+(\n|$)/` would at least catch if there's any numeric patterns for any of the rows. That might be enough.
bvaughn: Ah right. I forgot the `m` flag to make `/:\d+:\d+$/` function that way.
